another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'll help you determine if you can claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me start by asking: **How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of his exact age right now - he's a teenager, somewhere between 15 and 19. Does that matter for the claim?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, age does matter for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me explain:

- For children **under 16**, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for them and live in the UK.
- For children **aged 16 to 19**, you can still get Child Benefit, but only if they're in approved education or training.

So to assess Alex's eligibility properly, I need to know: **Is Alex under 16, or is he 16 or over? And if he's 16 or over, is he currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, or an approved training course)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I honestly don't know his exact age at the moment - I know he's somewhere in that 15 to 19 range, but I can't tell you for certain whether he's under or over 16 right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - you're not certain of Alex's exact age at the moment.

Let me ask some other questions that will help me assess eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - here in England - and yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:

**Are you responsible for Alex - meaning you're providing for his day-to-day needs like food, clothes, and other expenses?**

conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for him - I provide everything he needs day-to-day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:

- Is he currently in hospital or care?
- Has he started paid work for 24 hours or more per week?
- Is he claiming any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment Support Allowance)?
- Has he started an apprenticeship?

**What we know:**
